instruction: We want to extend our AWS Backup setup to protect a second S3 bucket and also add cross-region copy for disaster recovery. The current backup vault is {{reference-architectures-Backup-s3-us-east-1-BackupVaultName}} and it backs up {{reference-architectures-Backup-s3-us-east-1-BucketName}} under plan {{reference-architectures-Backup-s3-us-east-1-BackupPlanId}}. Review the current configuration: how does the backup plan select which resources to protect, what is the schedule and retention, and what encryption does the vault use? Based on this, explain what we need to do to add a second S3 bucket to the existing backup plan, and whether the current vault setup supports adding a cross-region copy rule.
expected_answer: The backup plan (id {{reference-architectures-Backup-s3-us-east-1-BackupPlanId}}) uses a tag-based selection: it targets all resources tagged daily-backup=true (condition: STRINGEQUALS). The plan has a single rule (DailyBackupRule) that runs daily at midnight UTC via cron(0 0 * * ? *) with a 35-day retention (DeleteAfterDays: 35), an 8-hour start window, and a 7-day completion window. The vault {{reference-architectures-Backup-s3-us-east-1-BackupVaultName}} is encrypted with the AWS-managed Backup KMS key (alias/aws/backup in the account) since no customer-managed CMK was specified. The vault is not locked. The existing S3 bucket {{reference-architectures-Backup-s3-us-east-1-BucketName}} has versioning Enabled and uses SSE-S3 (AES256) encryption. To add a second S3 bucket to the backup plan, you simply need to: (1) enable versioning on the new bucket, since AWS Backup requires versioning for S3 backups, and (2) add the tag daily-backup=true to it. The tag-based selection will automatically include any resource with that tag -- no changes to the backup plan or selection are needed. For cross-region copy, the current vault setup is compatible. You would add a CopyAction to the existing backup rule specifying a destination backup vault ARN in the target region. The destination vault will have its own KMS encryption key (either the AWS-managed default key in that region or a customer-managed CMK you create there). AWS Backup handles re-encryption during the copy process, so using the AWS-managed default key on the source vault does not block cross-region copy. No changes to the source vault encryption are required.
